questions.answer: E.m.f. is energy transferred by a source from other forms to electrical energy per unit charge driven around a complete circuit. Potential difference is energy transferred per unit charge.
accepted_alternatives: For e.m.f., accept energy supplied by a source per unit charge. For p.d., accept work done per unit charge.
questions.tolerance: Require energy per unit charge for both and distinguish source supply from component transfer.

marking_points.text: Defines e.m.f. as energy supplied or transferred by a source per unit charge
Defines potential difference as energy transferred or work done per unit charge

questions.unit_policy: No unit required beyond selecting one option.

marking_points.text: Selects C: terminal p.d. is less than e.m.f. because energy per unit charge is transferred inside the cell

option_feedback.A: Internal resistance transfers electrical energy to thermal energy; it does not give extra energy to charge.
option_feedback.B: For non-zero current and non-zero internal resistance, Ir is non-zero, so V is below the e.m.f.
option_feedback.C: Correct. Some source-supplied energy per coulomb is transferred inside the cell.
option_feedback.D: Charge is conserved. It is energy per unit charge that is transferred inside the cell.

questions.unit_policy: No unit required beyond selecting one option.

marking_points.text: Selects C by calculating V = 4.5 - (0.50 × 0.60) = 4.2 V

option_feedback.A: This is only the lost volts Ir, not the terminal p.d.
option_feedback.B: This subtracts r rather than Ir from the e.m.f.
option_feedback.C: Correct. Ir = 0.30 V and V = 4.5 - 0.30 = 4.2 V.
option_feedback.D: This adds lost volts to the e.m.f. for a discharging source.

questions.unit_policy: No unit required beyond selecting one option.

marking_points.text: Selects D: lower current makes Ir smaller, so V = 𝓔 - Ir increases

option_feedback.A: The question states that the e.m.f. stays constant.
option_feedback.B: A smaller subtracted value makes V larger, not smaller.
option_feedback.C: Current changes the internal voltage loss Ir.
option_feedback.D: Correct. Lower current reduces lost volts, so terminal p.d. rises toward the e.m.f.

questions.answer: Lost volts = Ir = 0.75 × 0.40 = 0.30 V. Terminal p.d. = 7.2 - 0.30 = 6.9 V. It is below the e.m.f. because 0.30 J per coulomb is transferred to thermal energy inside the cell.
questions.tolerance: Accept 0.30 V and 6.9 V only, subject to normal rounding display.

marking_points.text: Uses lost volts = Ir with I = 0.75 A and r = 0.40 Ω
Obtains 0.30 V
Uses V = 𝓔 - Ir or subtracts the 0.30 V internal loss from 7.2 V
Obtains 6.9 V

parts.label: (c)
parts.answer: Some source-supplied energy per unit charge is transferred to thermal energy in the internal resistance, leaving less energy per unit charge for the external circuit.
accepted_alternatives: The internal resistance has a potential difference Ir, so V = 𝓔 - Ir.
parts.tolerance: Require internal energy transfer or an equivalent lost-volts explanation.

marking_points.text: Explains that energy per unit charge is transferred inside the source, leaving terminal p.d. below e.m.f.

questions.answer: The internal voltage loss is 9.6 - 8.4 = 1.2 V, so r = 1.2/1.20 = 1.0 Ω. Internal power = I²r = 1.20² × 1.0 = 1.44 W, reported as 1.4 W to two significant figures.
accepted_alternatives: For internal power accept I(𝓔 - V) = 1.20 × 1.2 = 1.44 W.
questions.unit_policy: Internal resistance requires Ω and power requires W.
questions.tolerance: Accept r = 1.0 Ω and power from 1.4 W to 1.44 W.

marking_points.text: Finds the internal voltage loss as 9.6 - 8.4 = 1.2 V
Uses r = (𝓔 - V)/I with I = 1.20 A
Obtains 1.0 Ω
Uses Pinternal = I²r or I(𝓔 - V) with consistent values
Obtains 1.44 W, or 1.4 W to two significant figures

questions.answer: Some of the 12.0 J supplied per coulomb is transferred inside the battery, leaving a smaller terminal energy per coulomb. Normal mode: V = 12.0 - 0.50 × 0.80 = 11.6 V. Burst mode: V = 12.0 - 2.0 × 0.80 = 10.4 V. Source powers are 12.0 × 0.50 = 6.0 W and 12.0 × 2.0 = 24 W, so burst mode has greater source power.
questions.unit_policy: Terminal p.d. answers require V and power answers require W.
questions.tolerance: Accept 11.6 V, 10.4 V, 6.0 W and 24 W.

parts.label: (a)
parts.answer: The e.m.f. is the total energy supplied per unit charge. Some energy per unit charge is transferred to thermal energy in the internal resistance, so less remains for transfer in the external transmitter and terminal p.d. is lower.
parts.tolerance: Require both total source supply per unit charge and internal transfer per unit charge.

marking_points.text: Identifies e.m.f. as the total energy supplied by the battery per unit charge
Explains that some energy per unit charge is transferred in the internal resistance, leaving a lower terminal p.d.
Uses V = 𝓔 - Ir with I = 0.50 A and r = 0.80 Ω
Obtains 11.6 V
Uses V = 𝓔 - Ir with I = 2.0 A and r = 0.80 Ω
Obtains 10.4 V

parts.label: (d)
parts.answer: Pnormal = 𝓔I = 12.0 × 0.50 = 6.0 W and Pburst = 12.0 × 2.0 = 24 W. Burst mode has greater source power.
parts.tolerance: Accept 6.0 W and 24 W with burst mode identified.

marking_points.text: Uses source power P = 𝓔I to obtain 6.0 W in normal mode and 24 W in burst mode
States that burst mode has the greater source power
